      "partial_result": "**Verdict: conditional GO.** The seed design is sound. Fix the items below before any long training starts. The 3\u2011seed t\u2011gate is acceptable as a pre\u2011declared funding rule. It cannot count as seed inference, so it should not be the test R@1 has to pass.\n\n## Blocking corrections\n\n1. **Stop on any negative seed, not only at \u22120.002 / \u22120.0015.** Final GO already needs a nonnegative point effect on every seed. Once one seed is negative the outcome is KILL, so running the rest costs about 1,800s of GPU time for nothing. Stop the moment any R@1 or mAP@R point effect is below 0. Keep the rule to finish all three seeds when every seed is nonnegative.\n\n2. **Use the t\u2011interval only for mAP@R; do not gate R@1 with it.** Exact seed inference is impossible with n=3: even if all three seeds are positive, the best exact one\u2011sided sign or permutation p is 1/8 = 0.125. So the t\u2011interval (df2, t=4.303) is the only way to state 95% over seeds, and it depends entirely on assumptions. For it to pass, the mean must exceed about 2.5\u00d7 the seed SD.\n   - **mAP@R:** passing needs roughly mean \u2265 +0.005 with seed SD \u2248 0.002. Existing 1,000\u2011update native controls on a different panel (seeds 179024\u201327, mAP 0.8376\u20130.8419, so SD \u2248 0.002) make that plausible. It is consistent with the +0.005 floor, so keep it.\n   - **R@1:** the 100\u2011update effect was +0.44pp with a \u00b10.25pp conditional interval. A real effect of that size would probably fail the df2 lower bound. Make R@1 a non\u2011inferiority requirement instead: nonnegative on every seed and pooled product CI > 0.\n   - **Honest labelling:** state that both statistics are conditional on this one reused panel. The seed SD leaves out panel sampling variance.\n   - **If you want a distribution\u2011free seed claim:** it needs 5 seeds, all positive (exact one\u2011sided p = 1/32), about 9,000s. That is not worth it for a funding decision; state it as the upgrade path.\n\n3. **The real risk the gate must name is that the benefit may only be a head start.** The known 1,000\u2011update native controls score about 0.839 mAP and 98.5% R@1, versus 0.780 / 95.2% at 100 updates. That comparison is on a different panel: those receipts do not carry the 89f1dacd query or e7114b2c gallery digests. A basis+centre initializer typically speeds convergence and the gain may fade by step 1,000. The gate tests exactly this, which is right, but add it as the stated hypothesis. Also add a control validity floor: native at 1,000 updates must beat the 100\u2011update native (0.7799 / 95.25%), or the run is flagged as an invalid control.\n\n4. **Fix the text:** \"18,?00 queries\" should be **19,062** (3 \u00d7 6,354).\n\n## Minimal reuse implementation (no new modules)\n\n- **`train_inshop_siglip2_unseen_gallery.py`:**\n  - Seed choices at l.511: add 179028\u201330. Do the same in `preflight_inshop_siglip2_unseen_gallery.py:72`.\n  - l.537\u2013569: accept the 100 receipt SHA `d6f0d09d\u2026` as a third authority tier, with `updates == 1000` and seed in {179028,179029,179030}.\n  - Keep the existing 179024\u2011only branches as they are.\n  - The check at l.751 needs one new preflight receipt per seed. These run on CPU and freeze the schedule hashes before any GPU work, which is the pre\u2011freeze your gate asks for.\n- **Initializer guard:** the initializer uses all fit rows and should not depend on the seed. The 100\u2011update replay against the 17\u2011update smoke suggests it is deterministic. Assert that its digests for each new seed equal the ones in the 100 receipt. This is stronger than a smoke replay and costs nothing.\n- **Smokes:** code paths do not depend on the seed, and schedules come from the preflight. Run one 17\u2011update smoke pair, on 179028 only. Per\u2011seed smokes repeat the same test and add receipts to validate. The full run's first 17 steps should still be checked against it.\n- **`run_inshop_wide_head_100.py`:** make the hardcoded `\"179024\"` (l.123) and the update count parameters. Keep its parity, initializer\u2011equality (l.190) and bootstrap code unchanged.\n- **Aggregation:** a small CPU script over the three receipts.\n  - Pooled result: average per\u2011query deltas across seeds, since the query order is the same, and call the existing `bootstrap_lower(delta, qlabels)` from `score_inshop_crop_view_pair` (5,000 draws, seed 179019).\n  - Report each seed's effect, the pooled interval, and the mAP\u2011only t\u2011interval.\n  - Also record arm order, the early\u2011stop evaluation at each seed with its timestamp, and the SHA of each child receipt.\n- **Budget:** prior 1,000\u2011update freeze_emb runs trained in about 745s. Add about 109s of export and about 30s of overhead and each child is about 885s. That is under the 1,100s cap, and six children plus one smoke pair come to about 5,500s, under the 7,000s cap.\n\n## What a pass does and does not license\n\nA pass means only that this initializer is worth spending more on. It says nothing about SOTA, held\u2011out generalization or serving speed, because all three seeds reuse the same observed TRAIN split and panel.\n\nThe next qualification is one preregistered, frozen\u2011recipe run each on official In\u2011Shop query/gallery and SOP test. Use a single seed chosen in advance with no selection, and compare against the UNICOM\u2011family published numbers. Measure matched full\u2011image\u2011to\u2011top\u2011k serving latency on the new checkpoint in a separate cheap pilot first, then p99 only if the pilot works.",
